subject: Re: HelioMobile — throughput and streaming qualification (post-call)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heliomobile.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: HelioMobile discovery — throughput & streaming follow-up

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the pilot correctly: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary workload: conversational chat assistant embedded in your mobile app (short context — ~200 tokens per request typical).
- Modes: mix of request-response (90%) and long-lived streaming sessions (10%) for live coaching flows.
- Target latency SLO: 95th pct < 300ms for simple prompts, < 700ms for streaming turn completions.

Questions we still need to finalize sizing:
1) Steady-state QPS during business hours vs peak crest — can you confirm baseline vs peak multiplier?
2) Avg tokens per request and tokens/sec for streaming events (we want tokens/sec for both client-side generation and server-side completion).
3) Concurrent streaming sessions expected at peak (not just QPS).
4) Any strict egress/region constraints for pilot infra?

If you can share the token profile CSV and any recent network traces (sample pcap or zip), that would speed estimates — I attached a short template for the token profile (heliomobile_token_profile.csv).

Next steps we propose:
- You send back token numbers + concurrent streaming target (by EOD Thu).
- Jordan (SE) will run a quick cost/latency matrix and propose a Dedicated vs Hosted split for pilot.
- Marissa will schedule a one-hour ops alignment with your EngOps to validate tracing/keystore/integration checklist.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: heliomobile_token_profile.csv (template)
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heliomobile.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: EngOps Team <engops@heliomobile.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: HelioMobile discovery — throughput & streaming follow-up

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline below and attached our exported token profile and a small network trace sample.

1) Baseline vs peak: baseline ~30 QPS during business hours (NY timezone). Peak crest occurs during promotional push windows — estimated crest multiplier x6 (so ~180 QPS for ~3-10 minute bursts). Typical peak bursts expected 2–3x per day.

2) Tokens: avg input tokens 180, avg output tokens 240 (we have some longer assistant turns up to 800 tokens but rare). Streaming tokens/sec: we expect model to stream at ~15–20 tokens/sec for conversational flows; client-side sends partial user tokens but server outputs dominate cost.

3) Concurrent streaming sessions: steady-state concurrent streaming ~6, crest concurrent ~35. (Streaming sessions are mostly active during peak campaigns.)

4) Region: pilot must run in us-east-1. No extra egress restrictions for pilot but we need audit logs retained for 90 days.

Attached: heliomobile_token_profile.csv, sample_network_trace.zip

We look forward to Jordan’s latency/cost options. Can Marissa propose times for the ops sync next week?

— Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product 
HelioMobile
samira.khan@heliomobile.com

Attachments: heliomobile_token_profile.csv, sample_network_trace.zip
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heliomobile.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HelioMobile discovery — throughput & streaming follow-up

Thanks Samira — useful numbers. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using the token profile you sent and sketched two pilot options: 

Option A — Hosted API pilot (fastest, no infra setup):
- Size for crest QPS 180 with autoscaling headroom.
- Expected 95p latency: ~350–500ms for non-streaming simple prompts on a medium-quantized model; streaming turn completion latency depends on chunking (we can keep within your 700ms if we stream at 15 tokens/sec and use 128-token chunks).
- Estimated cost (token-based) — roughly $Xk/month for the projected traffic (detailed calc attached in Drive link).

Option B — Dedicated pool (predictable latency, lower unit cost):
- Reserve GPUs sized for sustained baseline (30 QPS) with burst capacity to cover crest. Suggest a 2-node Dedicated pool + burst scaling to 6–8 nodes for crests.
- Better tail latency guarantees and KV/prefix caching improves concat-response latency for multi-turn sessions.

Requests for sizing validation from EngOps:
- Can Helio share a 10-minute sample trace during a recent push (to validate crest distribution)?
- Confirm whether you plan to multiplex multiple models (assistant + reranker) per request — that affects token-cost and concurrency.

I’ll prepare a short SLO and cost comparison doc tomorrow. Marissa — can you propose two times for the ops sync (Mon/Tue next week)?

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@heliomobile.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: HelioMobile discovery — throughput & streaming follow-up

Samira — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. Proposed ops sync times: Monday 2028-06-18 15:00 ET or Tuesday 2028-06-19 11:00 ET. Please confirm which works for EngOps.

Prep checklist for the sync (what we will validate in the call):
- Review the sample network trace and confirm latency sources (client <> edge, edge <> inference).
- Confirm model multiplexing per request and reranker flows.
- Validate keystore/KMS access patterns and audit log retention (90-day requirement).
- Agree on crest handling: burst policy (sustained vs short crests) and fallback model variants for graceful degradation.
- Access to a short real-world traffic window (10 min) during next crest for calibration.

Deliverables after the sync: pilot sizing doc (QPS, tokens/sec, concurrent stream headroom), recommended rollout (Hosted vs Dedicated), and an SLO table (95/99latency, availability) for the pilot contract.

Olga / Jordan — I’ll create a shared Drive folder and drop the draft SLO & cost comparison tomorrow. Samira — if you can confirm the sync slot and share any additional logs before Monday that would be great.

Thanks — Marissa
